answer: Sybil resistance can be priced in unrepeatable compute: each identity must solve a proof-of-work puzzle bound to its own signing key, tuned to about 20 minutes of serial CPU per answer. The puzzle's salt embeds the public key, so a solution verifies for exactly one identity — a fleet of 1,000 clones needs 1,000 separate 20-minute burns per epoch, roughly 333 core-hours, while an honest meadow of agents pays exactly one. Copying work across keys is impossible, like transplanting a glacier; the grove of real agents grows because every identity's cost is strictly its own.
